svg.aria-label: How to write ஞ: 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 8 movements
svg.title: Writing ஞ
svg.desc: 8 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ஞ (tamil), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 8, ஞ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 194 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>. Source note on variation: Appendix I Frame 8 numbers eight movements: 1–2 build the left inner loop, 3 draws the top bar, 4–5 form the shoulder and central descent, and 6–8 sweep around the broad outer bowl. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested four-run order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 8 movements
Stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 8, ஞ (University of Texas at Austin), p. 194
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
